verdicts.why: In the metallurgical sense printed here, temper names a physical property of a metal and takes no side on it.
A cause can be good, bad, or lost; the word names an organised effort toward an end and leaves the judging to its modifiers.
A legal term of art for a court proceeding; it describes the proceeding without attitude.
A courtroom procedure named plainly; the word carries no attitude toward the objection or the objector.
A unit of temperature is pure measurement with nothing to judge.
A unit of angular measure; descriptive only.
Degree here is a neutral scale of seriousness (third-degree burn, first-degree murder); the gravity belongs to the referent, not to the word.
A mathematical term for the highest power of a polynomial; nothing to judge.
Hopping a bus or plane is informal and suggests a quick, casual trip, but that is register and meaning, not an attitude of approval or contempt toward the trip.
To jump across something is plain physical description.
Traversing in short flights is descriptive of the manner of travel, with no judgement of it.
A British insurance term (life assurance) that names a product without attitude.
Undergoing an injury or illness is a bad referent named in the plain word; suffer takes no side on the sufferer.
To undergo something is the plain verb for enduring it; the unpleasantness is the meaning, not an added attitude.
Being set at a disadvantage (the team suffered from the loss) is plain description of an outcome, not a judgement of anyone.
Getting worse in quality (his work suffered) states a decline without an attitude toward what declined.
Saying someone suffers from a tendency rather than has one casts the habit as an affliction, a defect to be pitied or deplored, which is a judgement beyond the gloss be given to.
Being concerned with something is plain description of an attitude, not an attitude toward the thing itself.
Taking care of or caring for something in the sense of being in charge of it is plain description of a duty.
Going toward a place (seek shelter) is formal in register but judges nothing about the destination.
Inquiring for something (seek an answer, seek redress) is plain description of the asking with no attitude.
Staying with someone as a guest is the everyday, unloaded word for it.
Coming to see someone in a professional capacity is plain description of the call.
Chatting socially is a regional informal usage but carries no judgement of the talk or the talkers.
Visiting a punishment upon someone is a biblical, formal construction whose unpleasantness lies in what is imposed, not in the word's attitude.
Being visited by an illness or misfortune names a bad referent in a formal but neutral word.
Want as extreme poverty is a bad referent named plainly and somewhat literarily; the word does not judge the poor.
A lottery drawing is a game mechanism named without attitude.
Drawing liquid or current from a source is plain technical description.
Moving a load by pulling is plain physical description.
